doc.title: Butch Cage and Robert Pete Williams Interview, 1967-05-13
doc.interviewee: Butch Cage and Robert Pete Williams

chapter: Cage on work songs, church and social life
title: Fiddlers' contests
summary: The interviewer asks about contests; Cage says he beat other players but never won a cup.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Did you ever go to these meetings where they have fiddlers and they all meet up and see which one can play? I know I have a pass yet. You never did? No. You don't try to cut him a new frock as they call it? I have one that come in there when I dance and try to play at me. Uh huh. But I'm lucky enough to beat them out. In New Orleans sometimes they'll have a couple of bands get together. And the one that wins gets a cup.
Yeah. Have you ever seen him get a silver cup for anything like that? No. No. No. No.
We didn't get that at that time.
They ain't gonna cheap you know.
Oh yeah. Yeah. Did you ever go to Westerfield? No. No. No. No. No. No. No.
No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No. No.

No. Did they do that up in Mississippi and different places in Louisiana? Yes, they do that. It wasn't why I didn't do that. Just come to each other's house. Not much, though, but they used to do it again. Who were some of the good musicians you knew like that?
